objects.description: Configuration struct for the Zopfli compressor. Controls verbosity, optimization iteration count, and block-splitting behavior. Used by all compress functions in this API. Default values are set via ZopfliInitOptions.
Enumeration selecting the output container/format for compression: gzip, zlib, or raw deflate. Consumed by ZopfliCompress.

functions.name: ZopfliInitOptions
functions.description: Initializes a ZopfliOptions struct with library-defined default values. Use this before customizing options or passing them to compression functions.
requirements: options must be a non-NULL pointer to writable ZopfliOptions storage.
Call before using the options with any compression function.
No memory allocation is performed; the caller owns the storage.

functions.name: ZopfliCompress
functions.signature: void ZopfliCompress(const ZopfliOptions* options, ZopfliFormat output_type, const unsigned char* in, size_t insize, unsigned char** out, size_t* outsize);
functions.description: Compresses the input buffer using the specified output format (gzip, zlib, or raw deflate) and appends the compressed bytes to a caller-managed dynamic output buffer. Designed for repeated appends; the function grows the output as needed and updates size.
requirements: options must point to a valid, initialized ZopfliOptions (e.g., initialized via ZopfliInitOptions).
output_type must be one of: ZOPFLI_FORMAT_GZIP, ZOPFLI_FORMAT_ZLIB, or ZOPFLI_FORMAT_DEFLATE.
in must point to at least insize readable bytes (if insize > 0).
out must be a non-NULL pointer to a dynamic buffer pointer; the buffer is (re)allocated by the function as needed.
outsize must be a non-NULL pointer to the size of the dynamic buffer; it is updated by the function.
Caller must free(*out) after final use of the accumulated output.
If starting from an empty buffer, initialize *out to NULL and *outsize to 0 before the first call.
The function appends to any existing data in *out; callers relying on this behavior must ensure *out and *outsize are consistent with the existing buffer.

functions.name: ZopfliGzipCompress
functions.signature: void ZopfliGzipCompress(const ZopfliOptions* options, const unsigned char* in, size_t insize, unsigned char** out, size_t* outsize);
functions.description: Compresses the input buffer into the gzip container format and appends the compressed data to the caller’s dynamic output buffer. Suitable for producing .gz-compatible streams.
requirements: options must point to a valid, initialized ZopfliOptions.
in must point to at least insize readable bytes (if insize > 0).
out must be a non-NULL pointer to a dynamic buffer pointer; the buffer is (re)allocated by the function as needed.
outsize must be a non-NULL pointer to the current size; it is updated by the function.
Caller must free(*out) after final use of the accumulated output.
If starting from an empty buffer, initialize *out to NULL and *outsize to 0 before the first call.
The function appends to any existing data in *out; callers relying on this behavior must ensure *out and *outsize are consistent with the existing buffer.

functions.name: ZopfliZlibCompress
functions.signature: void ZopfliZlibCompress(const ZopfliOptions* options, const unsigned char* in, size_t insize, unsigned char** out, size_t* outsize);
functions.description: Compresses the input buffer into the zlib container format and appends the compressed data to the caller’s dynamic output buffer. Produces zlib-wrapped DEFLATE streams suitable for APIs expecting zlib data.
requirements: options must point to a valid, initialized ZopfliOptions.
in must point to at least insize readable bytes (if insize > 0).
out must be a non-NULL pointer to a dynamic buffer pointer; the buffer is (re)allocated by the function as needed.
outsize must be a non-NULL pointer to the current size; it is updated by the function.
Caller must free(*out) after final use of the accumulated output.
If starting from an empty buffer, initialize *out to NULL and *outsize to 0 before the first call.
The function appends to any existing data in *out; callers relying on this behavior must ensure *out and *outsize are consistent with the existing buffer.

data_types.description: A byte buffer of any content and length. Not required to be valid text or structured data; may contain any 8-bit values including NUL bytes. Used directly as an input payload to compression functions.
